subject: health
title: Calm-Down Tools
about: Naming a big feeling first, then picking a tool to settle the body: belly breaths, counting to ten, squeeze and relax, a quiet break, drawing it out, a hug, and talking once calm. NC 1.MEH.1.1 and 1.MEH.1.3 (healthy ways to express feelings and cope); builds on My Feelings.
tip: Practice one tool while he is already calm, like smell the flower and blow out the candle, so it is ready when a big feeling comes.

cards.q: A big feeling comes. What is a good first step?
cards.note: Say it out loud: I feel angry. I feel worried. Naming a feeling helps it shrink.
Frustrated means something is hard and you want to give up. Everyone feels it sometimes.

cards.q: You take a belly breath. What moves in and out?
cards.note: Put a hand on your belly. Breathe in through your nose and feel it fill up like a balloon.

cards.q: Smell the flower, then blow out the candle. What are you practicing?
cards.note: Breathe in slowly through your nose, then out slowly through your mouth. Do it three times.

cards.q: You feel angry. You count slowly. What number do you count up to?
cards.note: Counting slowly to ten gives your body time to cool down.

cards.q: Squeeze your fists tight like a lemon. Then what?
cards.note: Squeeze for a few seconds, then let your hands go soft. Feel the difference.

cards.q: You feel upset. Where can you go to calm down?
cards.note: Many classrooms have a calm corner. At home it can be your bed or a soft chair.

cards.q: What can you say to ask for a calm-down break?
cards.note: Asking for a break is a strong, smart thing to do.

cards.q: Which one is a calm-down tool?
cards.note: Draw how the feeling looks. Big, scribbly and red is fine.

cards.q: You feel mad and wiggly. What can help your body?
cards.note: Moving your body uses up the mad energy.

cards.q: You ask your grown-up for a hug. How can a hug help you feel?
cards.note: It is okay to ask for a hug. It is also okay to say no thanks to one.

cards.q: Is it okay to cry when you feel sad?
cards.note: Crying is one way the body lets a feeling out. Big kids and grown-ups cry too.

cards.q: Does everyone have big feelings sometimes?
cards.note: Big feelings are normal. What matters is what you do with them.

cards.q: Feelings come and go, like what in the sky?
cards.note: A big feeling floats by like a cloud. It will pass.

cards.q: You tried a belly breath and still feel angry. What can you do?
cards.note: Count to ten, squeeze and relax, or take a break. You have lots of tools.

cards.q: You feel calm again. What can you do about the problem now?
cards.note: Calm first, then talk. Try an I-message: I feel sad when...
